Maya: Quick alert — seeing repeated OOMs on dedicated-gpu-pool-3 after this morning's kernel-selector rollout (commit 6a3f2b).
Samir: Are these only on long-context jobs? :eyes:
Maya: Mostly >10k token runs, but we picked up a handful at ~6k too. Crash traces show slab alloc spikes then kernel_select hot.
Leo: I pulled a crash VM and ran a quick pprof. Top looks like: kernel_select() ~41%, kv_slab_alloc ~28%, eviction_scan ~15%.
Samir: Any CI flags or perf jobs complaining?
Maya: CI perf job 'runtime/kv-throughput' showed a regression ~18% on the canary matrix earlier, but it passed functional tests.
Talia: Can you paste the pprof snippet?
Leo: Sure — pasted below (shortened):
```
$ go tool pprof -top /tmp/pprof.cpu 
kernel_select  41.2%
kv_slab_alloc  28.1%
eviction_scan  14.7%
other          16.0%
```
Maya: Logs from the failing host show repeated allocations where seqlen grows, then a sweep: `kv_eviction_scan` runs and memory climbs instead of reclaiming. Suspect the new kernel routing changes the hot-slab alignment, hurting eviction locality.
Dmitri: That matches my offline repro where swapping kernel routes increased miss rate on the LRU window by ~3x.
Samir: Can we bisect to the exact PR? What commits are in the rollout?
Maya: Rollout included: kernel-router refactor (PR #4391), batching heuristic tweak (PR #4387), and a small kv-evict tuning (PR #4399). Canary started at 09:30 UTC.
Talia: My vote: temporarily switch kernel-router back via remote-config flag if possible, to confirm. Reverting the whole rollout is heavier.
Samir: +1 for switchback. If that removes OOMs, we know kernel-router is culprit. If not, we'll revert kv-evict.
Leo: I tested toggling `runtime.kernel_router=v1` locally and the slab miss rate dropped ~60% in a small replay.
Maya: Can infra flip the flag on pool-3 canary?
infra-bot: Received flag change request: runtime.kernel_router -> v1 for pool-3. Scheduling change on 3 hosts.
Dmitri: Also, we should run a targeted bisect across commits 4387..4399. I can script a narrow bisect that deploys each commit to a single canary node and runs our longctx replay.
Talia: Add a guard: if mem_usage > 85% for 5m, auto-rollback to kernel_router v1. That will limit blast radius.
Maya: Agreed. Action items: 1) infra flip kernel_router on canary (infra) 2) Dmitri run bisect script (dmitri) 3) Leo collect pprof samples for each bisect step (leo) 4) Talia add auto-rollback guard (talia).
Samir: If the switchback eliminates OOMs, we'll schedule a targeted revert of the kernel-router refactor, and re-evaluate the batching change separately.
Leo: One more datapoint — the KV eviction profiler shows high fragmentation counters after the router change, which explains why eviction_scan isn't freeing contiguous slabs. We might need a one-line kv-allocator patch to coalesce free ranges as a hotfix.
Maya: Ok let's hold the full rollout until bisect completes. I'll open an incident and note rollout hold.
infra-bot: Rollout hold applied for release 6a3f2b on pools: dedicated-gpu-pool-3. Incident: INC-2026-178.
Samir: Thanks everyone. Keep updates here. If anyone finds a convincing repro that isolates kernel_select -> slab fragmentation, ping pager.
Dmitri: Starting bisect now, will iterate every 20m. Looping in on results shortly.
Talia: I'll add the auto-rollback w/ 5m guard in a small PR and request expedited review.
Maya: Filing postmortem draft now with links to pprof and the canary logs: https://internal.redwood/perf/incidents/INC-2026-178
Samir: :thumbsup:
